text_full: Great addition to my healthy bean brownies! Recipe included!. I am always looking to make regular meals healthier. I like to replace rice with cauliflower rice, replace white sugar with Stevia and use beans where ever I can. I used this sugar to replace half the sugar in a healthier homemade brownie pie recipe I have tweaked with the main ingredient being low sodium canned great northern beans. For all of you skeptics out there, don’t knock it until you try it. This recipe is one I found online however I have tweaked the ingredients and trust me: it will blow you socks off. Ingredients: 2 cans low sodium northern beans 1/3 cup cocoa powder 2/3 cup quick oats (keep whole or blend into a flour) 1/4 cup applesauce 1/2 tap salt 1 tbsp vanilla extract 1 cups sugar (half white/half agave insulin powder) 1 cup chocolate chips (half milk/half dark) Oil is to drizzle in (any oil works: grapeseed, olive, avocado, vegetable) Add all ingredients into a food processor and then on low. While on, slowly drizzle the oil into the food processor until the mixture is smooth then add in chocolate chips and then on high for a few minutes until everything is incorporated into a batter. Pour into a pre-greased 8 inch circle pan, cook for 25 minutes and then left cool in the refrigerator for 4+ hours. Slice and serve! It is best served warmed up with vanilla ice cream!

Scent is Overpowering. Let me start by saying I love french-milled soaps. I love scented soap. I love guest/sample size soaps. I adore the delightful concept and packaging design of this set. It was on my wish list and I received it as a gift. I was looking very forward to having these soaps to add some holiday cheer to my home. Here's what happened. The person that purchased it for me was so overwhelmed by the strong scent that he had to triple bag the box and store it in a vacant room until Christmas. Each soap is individually wrapped. They're wrapped in plastic. Then in a box. Then they're double bagged in two ziploc bags. Then placed in yet another box, wrapped with wrapping paper. The box was under my tree for two days, and scent still managed to seep out and perfume all the other gifts under the tree nearby - but not in a pleasant way. When this was unwrapped Christmas morning it was so unbelievably overpowering my eyes watered. I didn't even bother to look closely at them - I could not get them back inside their ziplocs fast enough. People got headaches and complained loudly.. The entire downstairs smelled like a soap factory instead of the fresh cinnamon rolls I baked for Christmas morning. The soaps are now safely contained in their hazmat bags and stored in the laundry room instead of the guest bath. :( I'm really kind of bummed about this because I was so excited about these soaps. I want to try them or at least take them out and smell each one on its own, but I'm afraid to now. Greenwich Bay, if you read these reviews: please, please, PLEASE turn the scent levels down several notches in the recipe for these soaps. I think the scent must develop stronger as the soaps "ripen" because it's just much too much. Way more than any other french milled soaps I own.

Works Well On Most Shoes. We had a few pair of shoes that needed cleaning, so we tried this set. WHAT IS THIS LIKE? This can be used on the dirty soles of the shoes as well as leather, or textile shoes. You slowly use the sponge/brush tip to slowly clean the shoe in a circular motion. Once the shoe is entirely cleaned, then you wet a sponge and wipe the shoe clean. HOW DOES THIS PERFORM? This works beautifully on leather shoes (tough ones, not the soft porous leather types), but there was one pair of textile shoes it did not work on as well as I had hoped. It still worked somewhat though. THE BOTTOM LINE For a versatile shoe cleaner that does clean shoes well- especially leather- this is handy to have on hand. Another option for straightening hair!. I straighten my hair almost every day - it's pretty much a must for me - so when I had the opportunity to try this hair brush straightener, I jumped at the thought of finding an easier, more convenient way to straighten my hair. The upside? It definitely does straighten my hair! If I divide my hair into sections (like I would with the straightener) and brush the small sections at a time, my hair does get straight (almost) as well as it does with the straightener. The downside? I had hoped this would be a quicker, easier solution than my straightener...and it just wasn't. I got ALMOST the same results in about the same amount of time. For me, it wasn't enough of a difference to switch from the use of my straightener on a permanent basis. My hair is medium thickness with a slight wave to it and I set the temperature at 450 degrees. I think I probably spent about 15 to 20 minutes with this brush straightener (the same amount of time I spend with my regular straightener). My hair has been difficult to straighten with some straighteners as well, so my hair could be part of the issue! If you are looking for a new way to straighten your hair and your hair is not difficult to straighten, I would definitely suggest giving it a try...maybe it'll work better than a straightener for you! The hair brush straightener is well-made, high quality, and as described. I was surprised that I didn't burn my head with the straightener, but it does have protections in place for that (anti-scalding tips). big, bold cobalt bottle of lemon essential oil - great. The Radha lemon essential oil is wonderful – a big bottle of very strong smelling lemon oil (not a sweet lemon, but a very ‘true’ lemon scent). I use a LOT of lemon oil for making homemade dish soap and cleaners, so the big 4 oz bottle is great. You don’t need many drops to get the effect. Lemon essential oil cuts grease really well, and leaves a really clean scent. I stopped using commercial cleaners a few years ago and it makes a huge difference – dishes are cleaner, laundry smells better, and my skin is less itchy (recipe below for dish soap). I also use lemon oil a lot to clean my oven – nothing else seems to be able to get it looking that clean. The radha bottles are a trademark cobalt blue, protecting the essential oils from light and UV rays which can deteriorate the liquid inside – this extends the life of the oil and keeps it more potent. Their droppers are always high quality, also. Ingredients • 1 ¾ cups boiling water • 1 Tbsp borax (I've used this for the past 2 years and it lasts forever: [[ASIN:B00AZ6IH68 Mule Team Borax and Arm & Hammer Super Washing Soda Variety Pack]]) • 1 Tbsp grated soap (I use nonscented Ivory) • 15-20 drops 100% pure essential oils Directions 1. Heat water to boiling. 2. Combine borax and grated bar soap in a medium bowl. Pour hot water over the mixture. Whisk until the grated soap is completely melted. 3. Allow mixture to cool on the countertop for 6-8 hours, stirring occasionally. Dish soap will gel upon standing. 4. Transfer to a squirt bottle, and add essential oils (if using). Shake well to combine * I received the radha essential oil for evaluation and review

A Strange Design, but Well-Made and Comfortable. I didn’t know exactly what to expect when I ordered these DEENRSEE Micro Modal Open Fly Dual Pouch Men’s Low Rise Boxers. Underwear with a circular opening in the front, behind a “separate mezzanine,” designed to separate the wheat from the chaff, so to speak? I had no idea such things even existed until these showed up in my Vine queue. But I was intrigued enough to click the “Request Product” button. I’m glad I did. The concept behind this underwear is a little weird, but the execution is flawless. The material is extremely soft and smooth, almost satiny, and virtually frictionless. The quality is exceptional, with tight seams (including those around the all-important aforementioned aperture) and no open or missed stitches; these boxers seem well made and durable. As for comfort; well, YMMV, but I found the “unusual” and “interesting” configuration of the crotch area surprisingly innocuous and almost—but not completely—unnoticeable when worn. ‘Nuf said. My only slight gripe is that the sizing information is off a little. My waist measurement puts me right in the sweet spot of the “Medium” size range, so that’s what I ordered, and they’re a little too large to fit perfectly. They still fit all right, but they’re a little looser than I prefer. They seem to run a bit big, so consider that when you order. I like these boxers a lot, and this four-pack gives me an excuse to finally get rid of a few pairs of my ancient, threadbare, Jockey-style briefs. I’ve seen the future of men’s underwear, and it has a “separate mezzanine!”
